answer: Each identity must prove bank-account ownership: link an account in the applicant's legal name, then report back two random micro-deposits under one dollar within 48 hours, plus a matching utility bill. Opening a fresh bank account per fake identity forces real-world KYC, branch visits and fees, so the cost of a ripple of sockpuppets rises with each one. A tide of automated signups hits the deposit delay, and one account cannot serve two identities. Like shale, it forms slowly. Limits: it excludes unbanked people, and a stolen account could pass once, so add device binding.
